e7_s4_rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and fundus examination showing few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa. The progressive nature of the disease is also supported by lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Choroideremia
e7_s4_rejected.why: Choroideremia typically presents with more severe visual impairment and earlier loss of visual acuity, which is not seen in this patient.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Gyrate atrophy is characterized by well-defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy, which are not described in this patient's fundus examination.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Leber congenital amaurosis typically presents with severe visual impairment and nystagmus in early childhood, which is not consistent with this patient's symptoms and visual acuity.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Cone-rod dystrophy typically presents with decreased visual acuity and color vision defects, which are not seen in this patient, as color vision is normal and visual acuity is relatively preserved.
